connections.why: Factor, multiple and prime ideas rest on confident integer arithmetic
Percentages are hundredths, so fraction skills underpin percentage work
Converting to a common form lets fractions, decimals and percentages be ordered
Standard form expresses numbers using powers of ten
Surds arise from roots that cannot be written as exact decimals
Algebra generalises the arithmetic of numbers into symbolic manipulation
Manipulating expressions is needed to build and rearrange formulae
Expanding and factorising expressions is the key to solving equations
Inequalities are solved with the same balancing methods as equations
A linear equation in two variables is the equation of a straight line
Straight lines are the simplest graphs of equations on the coordinate plane
Understanding line equations leads to transforming whole curves
Function notation describes the relationships that graphs represent
A ratio of parts can be read as a fraction of the whole
Direct proportion is a constant ratio between two quantities
Compound interest is repeated percentage change over time
Similar shapes have lengths in direct proportion through a scale factor
Polygon angle properties build on angle rules at points and on lines
Circle theorems are statements about angles within a circle
Vector magnitude uses Pythagoras from triangle mensuration
Trigonometric and Pythagorean answers are often left in surd form
Rate-of-change graphs visualise growth and decay relationships
Proportional reasoning underlies representative and stratified sampling
Summary statistics are read from the charts that represent the data
Relative frequency from data estimates experimental probability
